evals.prompt: I need to add webhook support to our event system — when certain events fire (user.created, order.completed, payment.failed), we should POST a JSON payload to registered webhook URLs. we already have an event bus in src/events/ but no outbound webhook delivery yet. needs retry logic and a way for users to register their endpoints via the API
evals.expected_output: The skill should parse this as a well-specified feature request, assess confidence, potentially ask 1-2 clarifying questions about edge cases (retry policy, auth for webhook registration, payload format), write feature_spec to blackboard, then proceed to Phase 2 codebase exploration with multiple explorer instances.
expectations: The skill starts with Phase 0.0 configuration check
A team is created with TeamCreate (team_name containing 'feature-dev')
A blackboard is created for context sharing
Phase 1 begins with confidence assessment of the feature description
The skill identifies this as a reasonably well-specified request (mentions events, webhook URLs, retry logic, API endpoint) but asks clarifying questions about gaps
Clarifying questions target practical gaps: retry policy details, authentication/authorization for webhook registration, payload schema, failure thresholds, or rate limiting
A feature_spec is written to the blackboard before Phase 2
Phase 2 spawns multiple code-explorer instances (default 3) with different exploration focuses
Explorer instances are named with numbered suffixes (e.g., code-explorer-1, code-explorer-2)

evals.expected_output: This is a deliberately vague request. The skill should recognize low confidence and enter the elicitation loop, asking multiple rounds of questions to understand scope, what 'dark mode' means for this project, which components are affected, persistence strategy, etc.
expectations: The skill recognizes this as an underspecified request (cannot achieve 95% confidence from 2 words)
The first elicitation round asks about problem statement, scope, and what 'dark mode' means in context
Questions cover at least 3 of these dimensions: scope boundaries, user-facing behavior, integration points, persistence strategy, existing theming infrastructure
The skill does NOT proceed to Phase 2 without at least one round of user clarification
The skill uses AskUserQuestion (not just text output) to collect user input
After user responds, the skill re-assesses confidence before deciding whether to ask more questions

evals.prompt: I want to implement rate limiting middleware for our Express API. Should support per-route configuration (some endpoints like /health should be unlimited, auth endpoints should be strict like 5/min, and general API should be around 100/min). Use Redis for the token bucket counters since we already have a Redis connection in src/config/redis.ts. The middleware should return 429 with a Retry-After header when rate is exceeded. Needs to work with our existing auth middleware chain in src/middleware/
evals.expected_output: This is a very detailed request that should achieve near-95% confidence quickly. The skill should recognize the high level of specification, potentially ask only 1 question about minor gaps, write a comprehensive feature_spec, and move briskly to exploration.
expectations: The skill assesses this as a highly specified request (mentions technology, config pattern, existing infrastructure, HTTP behavior, integration points)
Confidence assessment is high — the skill either proceeds directly or asks at most 1 round of minor clarifying questions
The feature_spec captures: per-route config, Redis token bucket, 429 + Retry-After, integration with existing middleware
The skill does NOT over-elicit — it respects that the user has already provided detailed requirements
Phase 2 exploration focuses are tailored to the specific feature: one explorer for existing middleware patterns, one for Redis usage patterns, one for route configuration patterns

evals.prompt: /feature-dev --autonomous add a REST endpoint for user preferences that supports GET, PUT, and DELETE with validation and proper error responses
evals.expected_output: The skill should parse --autonomous, go through normal Phases 1-4 (elicitation, exploration, clarification, architecture), then use the autonomous convergence loop for Phase 5 implementation. Tests should be MUTABLE (not frozen).
expectations: The --autonomous flag is parsed and autonomous_mode is set to true
Phase 1 elicitation proceeds normally (95% confidence protocol)
Phase 2 codebase exploration proceeds normally with multiple explorer instances
Phase 4 architecture design proceeds normally with user selection
Phase 5 uses the autonomous convergence loop (not standard implementation)
Tests are MUTABLE: refactor-test MAY create and modify tests during iterations
Baseline snapshot is created after Phase 4 (architecture chosen) before implementation
Convergence-reporter is spawned at loop finalization

evals.prompt: /feature-dev --autonomous --iterations=15 implement OAuth2 PKCE flow for our SPA with token refresh and session management
evals.expected_output: The skill should parse both flags, set max_iterations to 15, and use the autonomous convergence loop for Phase 5. Phases 1-4 should proceed with interactive gates.
expectations: autonomous_mode is true, max_iterations is 15
Interactive gates are preserved: Phase 1 elicitation, Phase 3 clarification, Phase 4 architecture selection
Phase 5 approval gate asks about autonomous mode specifically
Score weights are loaded from config.autonomous.scoreWeights
The convergence loop includes keep/discard gating with git branch snapshots

evals.prompt: /feature-dev --autonomous add a simple health check endpoint that returns {"status": "ok"}
evals.expected_output: The skill should handle autonomous mode with a trivially simple feature. Tests should be mutable (can be created during iterations), unlike refactor mode where they are frozen.
expectations: The skill correctly identifies this as a simple feature and scales instance counts down
Phase 5 autonomous mode explicitly allows test creation: 'tests are MUTABLE'
refactor-test tasks include permission to create new test files
This contrasts with refactor autonomous mode where tests are FROZEN
The convergence loop may reach perfect score quickly on a simple feature
User approval is requested before starting autonomous implementation

evals.prompt: add spec compliance validation to the CLI output parser
evals.expected_output: Regression test for Phase 0.1 initialization stall. The skill MUST complete ALL three Phase 0.1 steps in strict order: TeamCreate → blackboard_create → TaskCreate×7. The agent must not stall after blackboard creation — it must immediately proceed to creating the 7 phase tasks and then begin Phase 1 elicitation.
expectations: Step 0.1.1: TeamCreate is called FIRST with team_name containing 'feature-dev' — this is a blocking prerequisite
Step 0.1.2: blackboard_create is called AFTER TeamCreate succeeds (not before, not without TeamCreate)
Step 0.1.3: TaskCreate is called 7 times AFTER blackboard_create succeeds — one for each phase (Discovery, Exploration, Clarifying Questions, Architecture, Implementation, Quality Review, Summary)
The agent does NOT stall between blackboard_create and TaskCreate — there is no pause, no extended thinking, no waiting
All 7 TaskCreate calls complete before the agent moves to Phase 1
Phase 1 elicitation begins after all Phase 0.1 steps complete — the agent asks clarifying questions about 'spec compliance validation' and 'CLI output parser'
The agent does NOT skip TeamCreate and jump directly to blackboard_create
If any Phase 0.1 step fails, the agent reports the error clearly rather than silently stalling

evals.prompt: implement a retry queue for failed background jobs with exponential backoff and dead letter support
evals.expected_output: Regression test verifying the full Phase 0 → Phase 1 transition completes without stalling. The initialization sequence (config check, TeamCreate, blackboard, task creation) must flow without interruption into the elicitation phase.
expectations: Phase 0.0: Config file is loaded or created with defaults before any swarm operations
Phase 0.1.1: TeamCreate is the FIRST swarm operation — called before any blackboard or task operations
Phase 0.1.2: blackboard_create is called with a scope-slug derived from the feature description (e.g., 'feature-dev-retry-queue-for-failed-background')
Phase 0.1.3: All 7 phase tasks are created via TaskCreate — the agent does not stop at fewer than 7
The transition from Phase 0 to Phase 1 is seamless — no stall, no repeated tool calls, no empty outputs
Phase 1 confidence assessment begins immediately after Phase 0 completes
The agent correctly assesses this as a moderately specified request and asks clarifying questions about backoff parameters, dead letter thresholds, job types, and persistence strategy
